prompt:
Produce exactly one concise caption (one sentence) containing 2–6 discrete visual facts separated by semicolons. Facts must appear in this strict priority order when present: 
1) legible text (transcribe exact words in double quotes, preserving capitalization and punctuation; omit if any characters are illegible); 
2) counts and object types (use numerals, e.g., "2 people", prefer canonical nouns); 
3) key color / material / condition adjectives placed immediately before the noun (e.g., "orange extension ladder", "rusted metal roof"); 
4) pose / action / orientation (e.g., "holding", "bending over", "looking left"); 
5) simple spatial layout using foreground / midground / background and left/right; 
6) lighting / viewpoint / occlusion cues (e.g., "bright sunlight casting long shadows", "tree partially obscures façade"). 

Rules:
- Use semicolons to separate facts; produce exactly one sentence with 2–6 facts; do not produce lists, tags, multiple sentences, or extra commentary.  
- If text is legible, quote the exact text (e.g., Sign reads "OPEN"); do not paraphrase or guess partial words.  
- Use numerals for counts (e.g., "2 people"). Use short canonical object names; place color/material adjectives immediately before the noun.  
- When more than one person/object is present, include at least one visually verifiable distinguishing attribute for each (clothing color/type, accessory, hair, glasses) and associate it with left/right or foreground/midground if visible; if no distinguishing attribute is visible, state only the count and location.  
- Do not infer roles, occupations, emotions, intentions, or use metaphors, slogans, or marketing language. Do not guess unreadable text or unconfirmed object classes—omit unsupported facts rather than hedge ("appears", "maybe").  
- Preserve punctuation and case for any transcribed text. Internally verify each fact is visually supported before output.

Compact canonical guidance (use when visually supported): step ladder = short hinged ladder with spreader bars; extension ladder = long multi-section ladder; backpack = bag with shoulder straps; if unsure, prefer a safe generic class only when visually evident (e.g., "bag" rather than a specific subtype).

Good / Bad examples (each is a single-sentence caption; facts separated by semicolons):
Good: Sign reads "Outdoor World"; 2 adults walk toward the store entrance; timber façade and concrete forecourt; overcast sky.
Bad: A happy farmer enjoys a sunny day in the countryside.
Good: Sign reads "SUBWAY"; person in green shirt bends over a pile of bags; tree trunk in foreground; bright sunlight casting sharp shadows.
Bad: People outside a restaurant having a nice time in the sun.
Good: 1 woman wearing a light-blue apron with large silver hoop earrings sits in foreground; plastic bags and stacked cardboard boxes in background; seated, facing forward.
Bad: A vendor smiling in a messy store.
Good: 2 people stand in a hallway; right person holds a red cup; left person gestures with open hands; wooden floor in foreground; recessed lighting overhead.
Bad: Two friends chatting with stickers on the wall.

Produce exactly one caption sentence that follows the rules above and nothing else.
